examples.text: Als het even kan moet 24 uur per dag worden geobserveerd wanneer de dieren aan- en afvliegen, wat de activiteiten op het nest zijn en welke prooien er worden aangevoerd. Ook het roepen van het mannetje en het vrouwtje wordt bijgehouden.

glosses: To go missing; to become a missing person.

examples.text: Eighteen years after Jaycee Dugard disappeared in 1991, she was found alive in the summer of 2009.

glosses: To go away; to become lost.

examples.text: I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields[…]. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair,[…]. My client welcomed the judge […] and they disappeared together into the Ethiopian card-room, which was filled with the assegais and exclamation point shields Mr. Cooke had had made at the sawmill at Beaverton.
A turban and loincloth soaked in blood had been found; also a staff. These properties were known to have belonged to a toddy drawer. He had disappeared.

glosses: To make vanish; especially, to abduct or murder for political reasons.

examples.text: The Chinese government is well-known for disappearing particularly vocal political dissidents.

"Did they disappear him?"
 "I don’t know."
 "What will you do if they decide to disappear you?"
Now a new hunt is under way to find a grave believed to contain the remains of some of those who were “disappeared” at Colonia Dignidad.
"It's such an honoring for Native people in this country, when we've been so disappeared and disregarded," Harjo says.
The book centres on Eilish Stack, a scientist, mother of four and wife to a teacher trade unionist who has been disappeared by the secret police.
Yet after her brother was detained and disappeared by Israeli forces at a checkpoint as he evacuated south months ago, Ms. Nabil, like others, fears moving south.

glosses: To travel by airplane to a destination.

examples.text: I'm going to fly out to see you.

glosses: To have someone travel rapidly to a destination on an airplane.

examples.text: flew him out to New York

glosses: To take off from an airfield.

examples.text: Near by is the RAF museum at Duxford Airfield, open at weekends, which has a large display of aircraft. Trapped there is the prototype Concorde, which flew in but can never fly out, because the runway was shortened to make way for a motorway immediately after its arrival.
Pieces flew out in all directions.

glosses: To become out by hitting a fly ball which is caught.

examples.text: Jones flied out to right field.

glosses: To fly into a rage; to become very angry.

examples.text: A fly out was recorded on the scorecard.

glosses: To flee rapidly; to run away.
To be spurred into ranting, shouting or otherwise agitated speaking.
